title: Design system, persistent chrome, landing page, and Method and sources page

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL PASS â€” QA1 audit round 1, Sprint 11, commit d735884 (HEAD), clean
tree for every audited path (the only dirty file is sprint-7's definition,
unrelated). Sprint file read fresh and in full, including Dev Notes, before
this verdict. CLAUDE.md re-read at this commit, since this diff amends it.

Two required fixes, both to Dev Notes, no code change. The build itself is
sound and the two things most likely to have gone wrong â€” the statute guard
being decorative, and the global stylesheet quietly undoing Sprints 8-10 â€”
did not go wrong.

SCOPE LIMIT
This is a static audit. I did not open a browser. Visual regression on
`/intake`, contrast ratios, phone-width reflow and print behaviour are gate
2's, with real instruments. Announcements are gate 3's. Legal content and the
authored copy are gate 4's. Where I comment on visual effects below I am
reading CSS selectors and specificity out of the source, not looking at a
rendered page, and I say so.

===================================================================
THE ELEVEN GATE-1 CHECKS
===================================================================

1. `classical.css` IMPORTED ONCE, GLOBALLY â€” PASS. `app/layout.tsx:7`,
   `import "./classical.css"`, after `./globals.css`. Exactly one import
   repo-wide (the only other match is a comment in DisclaimerBanner).

2. NO HARD-CODED HEX OR TOKEN-DUPLICATING px â€” PASS, verified rather than
   assumed. Grepped every new and modified component for `#rrggbb`: zero hits.
   Every colour goes through `var(--color-*)`. Grepped for literals equal to
   the declared spacing scale (4.6/9.2/13.8/18.4/27.6/36.8px) and the radius
   tokens (2/4/7px): zero hits. `var(--space-6)`, `var(--color-divider)`,
   `var(--color-accent)` and `var(--font-heading)` are used where tokens
   exist. The stylesheet declares no font-size token, so the inline `15px`,
   `19px`, `42px` etc. re-derive nothing that exists.

   Observation, not a finding: `/about` and the landing page are styled almost
   entirely through inline `style={{}}` objects rather than the `.card`,
   `.field`, `.tag` component layer. That is not what any criterion forbids
   and every value routes through tokens, so it passes as written. It is worth
   knowing that the component-class layer this sprint landed is, on these two
   pages, largely unexercised â€” a design-system adherence question for
   whoever owns the next screen, not a gate-1 defect.

3. CLAUDE.md UPDATED IN THE SAME DIFF â€” PASS. The Stack table row is amended
   and a two-paragraph split is added below it, naming which system owns what
   (`classical.css`: global element defaults plus its component-class layer,
   for chrome/landing/`/about`; Tailwind: `/intake`, untouched) and which wins
   on conflict. The specificity reasoning is correct: a Tailwind utility is a
   class selector (0,1,0) and beats `classical.css`'s bare-element type
   selectors (0,0,1) regardless of load order. Requirement 2 satisfied. See
   issue 1 for where that paragraph is incomplete rather than wrong.

4. NO FILE IMPORTS `lib/guide.ts` â€” PASS, and enforced rather than promised.
   Grep across `app/`, `components/` and `lib/` returns nothing.
   `lib/guide-import-boundary.test.ts` walks all three trees and asserts the
   absence per file, so requirement 10 is now a test rather than a
   convention â€” the right instinct, and it will catch the next person who
   reaches for the file without reading the sprint. Its regex covers
   `@/lib/guide`, `../guide` and `./guide`; a dynamic `import()` or `require`
   would slip past, which is worth knowing but is not the realistic case.

5. THE STATUTE GUARD FAILS CLOSED â€” PASS, and this is the strongest work in
   the diff. `checkStatuteCitationGuard` takes `unknown`, and every path that
   is not an exact match returns `{ passed: false, reason }`: empty library,
   non-object, null, missing or empty id, id absent from the library, and â€”
   the one that matters â€” an id that matches while `statute` or `section` text
   has drifted. No throw, no swallow, no default-pass branch. The result type
   is a discriminated union, so `result.reference` is unreachable on the
   failure branch by construction rather than by discipline. It mirrors
   `checkCitationGuard`'s double-check, which is the model requirement 7 named.

6. `STATUTE_REFERENCE_LIBRARY` EXPORTED, AND `/about`'s REFERENCES RESOLVE
   THROUGH IT â€” PASS. Named export, `readonly StatuteReference[]`, four
   entries. `app/about/page.tsx` maps every row through the guard and renders
   `result.reference` on success â€” the verified library entry, never the
   candidate â€” and on failure renders a visible "Reference withheld â€”
   verification mismatch" notice in place of the row. That is a real consumer,
   not a guard sitting beside the render path.

   The detail that makes it real: `REQUESTED_SOURCES` is authored as
   independent literals rather than imported from the library, so the guard
   can actually fail. Importing the library and checking it against itself
   would have been a no-op that looked identical in a diff. Dev Notes says so
   and the page carries the same comment. That is the difference between a
   guard and a decoration, and someone thought about it.

7. NO DOMAIN-SHAPED INTERFACE OUTSIDE `lib/types.ts` â€” PASS for this sprint's
   own code; see issue 2 for `lib/guide.ts`, which is a scoping question
   rather than a defect. `StatuteReference` went into `lib/types.ts` with a
   doc comment. The only other declarations in new code are `IconProps`
   (`{ size?, className? }` â€” a component prop bag, not domain-shaped) and
   `StatuteCitationGuardResult`, which sits beside its guard exactly as
   `CitationGuardResult` sits in `lib/citation-guard.ts`. I checked that
   precedent rather than taking Dev Notes' word for it; it holds.

8. `aria-current` WIRED FROM THE ACTIVE ROUTE â€” PASS.
   `components/Nav.tsx` uses `usePathname()` and sets
   `aria-current={pathname === link.href ? "page" : undefined}`. Strict
   equality, so `/` does not match `/intake` as a prefix and exactly one link
   can carry it. `undefined` rather than `"false"`, so the attribute is absent
   rather than present-and-negative. `classical.css:228` styles
   `.nav a[aria-current='page']`, so the accessibility attribute and the
   visual state cannot drift apart.

9. DECORATIVE NUMERALS HIDDEN â€” PASS. Both sets carry `aria-hidden="true"`,
   and both sites are inside `.map()` calls so every instance is covered:
   `app/page.tsx:128` for the `01`/`02`/`03` panel ordinals and
   `app/page.tsx:203` for the ghost Roman numerals (confirmed `opacity: 0.22`,
   matching requirement 9's description). Both icons in `components/icons.tsx`
   are also `aria-hidden`, which is correct for decorative SVG.

10. VITEST GREEN, REQUIREMENT 11's CASES PRESENT, NO RENDER-ASSERTION TEST â€”
    PASS. 16 files, 110/110, up from 63 as Dev Notes states. `tsc --noEmit`
    and `eslint .` both exit 0. The statute-guard suite has eight cases
    covering all three required scenarios and more: a listed reference passes,
    an unlisted id is withheld, drifted text for a matching id is withheld,
    three malformed-input cases (null, string, missing id), an empty library,
    and a duplicate-id check on the real library. No render test and no
    `jsdom`/`happy-dom`/`@testing-library` anywhere in `package.json` or the
    vitest config. The import-boundary test reads source text and renders
    nothing.

11. NO FILE UNDER `app/intake/` MODIFIED â€” PASS. `app/intake/page.tsx` is
    untouched, and so is `components/IntakeFlow.tsx`, where the intake markup
    actually lives. Worth noting for the record that the criterion names only
    `app/intake/`; the substantive file is in `components/`, and it is clean
    too, so the criterion's intent is met as well as its letter.

    I also checked the risk the sprint named but nobody reported on: whether
    intake markup happens to use any of `classical.css`'s component-class
    names, which would change its behaviour with no line of its code edited.
    I extracted all 36 class selectors from the stylesheet and searched
    intake's `className` attributes for each. **No collisions.** `.radio`,
    `.seg`, `.card`, `.input`, `.field`, `.btn` and the rest appear nowhere in
    intake. That risk did not materialise, and it is better recorded as
    checked than left silent.

===================================================================
ISSUE 1 â€” THE REQUIREMENT-8 FINDING IS UNDERSTATED [required fix]
===================================================================

Requirement 8's design is that stylesheet damage to `/intake` gets **raised as
a finding, not absorbed**. Dev Team did raise one, which is the right
behaviour. The problem is its scope: it describes a font-family shift and then
says colours are safe, and the source does not support the second half.

Dev Notes, verbatim: "`/intake`'s typography visibly shifted â€” labels,
options, and body text now render in `classical.css`'s serif body font
(Lora)... **Colors and explicit Tailwind utility classes (e.g. the primary
button's `bg-blue-700`) are unaffected**, since those are class selectors that
still win locally."

The second clause is true only of elements that carry an explicit Tailwind
class for the property in question. `classical.css` reaches every route with
these bare-element rules, all of which apply to intake:

- `body { color: var(--color-text); font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.55 }`
  (line 90) â€” inherited colour, size and leading, not only font-family.
- `h1..h6 { font-family: var(--font-heading); font-weight: ... }` and
  per-level `font-size` (lines 91-101).
- `p { margin: 0 0 var(--space-3) }` (line 102) â€” a bottom margin where
  Tailwind's preflight previously set none.
- `a { color: var(--color-accent) }` (line 103).

The concrete case, which is a size change rather than a family change:
`components/IntakeFlow.tsx:760` is
`<h2 className="font-medium text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50">` â€” the
duty-to-accommodate section heading. It carries no text-size utility.
`classical.css:96` sets `h2 { font-size: 32px }`, and Tailwind's preflight
neutralises heading sizes with a type selector of equal specificity that now
loads first, so `classical.css` wins. That heading goes from roughly body size
to 32px in Cormorant Garamond. By contrast `IntakeFlow.tsx:849`'s `<h1>` does
carry `text-2xl` and is protected â€” which is exactly the rule Dev Notes
states, applied consistently, and it is why the h2 case should have surfaced.

I am reading selectors and specificity, not a rendered page. Whether this
reads as "shifted" or "broken" is GroundTruth's call with an actual browser,
and requirement 8 does not ask Dev Team to fix it. What it asks is that the
finding be raised, and a finding that says "typography shifted to serif,
colours unaffected" points GroundTruth and Chang at less than is there.

FIX: restate the requirement-8 finding to cover the full set of bare-element
rules that reach `/intake`, name the `h2` at IntakeFlow.tsx:760 as a concrete
size change, and drop or qualify "colours are unaffected" â€” explicitly classed
elements are protected, unclassed ones inherit `--color-text` and links take
`--color-accent`.

The same gap exists in the CLAUDE.md paragraph, which frames the `/intake`
effect purely as *inherited* defaults ("an element with no explicit Tailwind
font utility inherits `classical.css`'s serif body font"). The `h2` case is a
direct type-selector match, not inheritance. The ownership sentence above it
does say `classical.css` owns "`h1`-`h6` sizing/weight", so a careful reader
can derive it â€” but this is the standards file, and CLAUDE.md's own warning is
that agents will audit against whatever it says. Worth one clause there too.

===================================================================
ISSUE 2 â€” `lib/guide.ts` WAS COMMITTED AND DEV NOTES NEVER SAYS SO
===================================================================

`lib/guide.ts` is **newly added** in this commit â€” 428 lines, previously
untracked (confirmed absent from tree 3e20931). It declares exactly the twelve
domain-shaped types requirement 10 describes: `Concern`, `ConcernId`,
`PathId`, `FactorId`, `DeadlineKey`, `PathStep`, `Framework`, `Bullet`,
`GuidePath`, `DeadlineRow`, `Answers`, `Recommendation`. `Answers` in
particular names the same concept as the intake's own answer shape, which is
the drift scenario CLAUDE.md's domain-types rule exists to prevent.

It is the largest file in the diff, this sprint forbids importing it, and Dev
Notes â€” which is otherwise unusually thorough, down to explaining icon
substitution â€” does not mention adding it to version control at all.

WHY THIS IS NOT A FAIL. Gate 1's criterion says "no domain-shaped interface is
declared outside `lib/types.ts`," and read alone this diff violates it twelve
times. But requirement 10 and the Out of Scope section address this exact file
by name: relocation "belongs to the sprint that first needs the file," and Out
of Scope says it belongs to "the sprint that first **imports** the file" â€” a
sentence that only makes sense if the file persists in the repository across
sprints. The specific, deliberate carve-out governs the general criterion, and
none of this sprint's own code declares a domain type outside `lib/types.ts`.
Committing the handoff artifacts alongside `app/classical.css` and
`docs/design-handoff.md` is also the only way an untracked file survives to be
relocated later.

FIX: record it in Dev Notes. One paragraph â€” that `lib/guide.ts` is committed
as a handoff artifact, that it is knowingly unimported, that its twelve types
are the deferred relocation requirement 10 and Out of Scope name, and that
`lib/guide-import-boundary.test.ts` is the enforcement. A 428-line file
entering the repo under a requirement that forbids using it should not be
something the next reader discovers from `git show --stat`.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER, not blocking this verdict. The gate-1 criterion and the
requirement-10 deferral now point different ways, because as of this commit the
file is in the repository rather than merely "on disk" as the Context section
assumed. I have read the deferral as governing and said why. That reading
should be written into the sprint file rather than left for the next auditor
to re-derive, because the next one may reasonably decide the other way â€” and
per Sprint 10's Amendment 1, a criterion that fires on something the same
document deliberately permits is the kind of thing that gets settled by
amendment, not by an auditor's judgement.

===================================================================
OBSERVATIONS â€” NO ACTION
===================================================================

- `components/DisclaimerBanner.tsx` renders
  `className="disclaimer no-print sticky top-0 z-50"`, mixing the
  `classical.css` class layer with Tailwind utilities inside one component â€”
  which the CLAUDE.md paragraph this same diff adds calls "what this split
  exists to avoid." I am not raising it as a fix: `.disclaimer`
  (classical.css:264) sets no positioning, so the three utilities supply
  behaviour the stylesheet does not have and preserve Sprint 1's sticky
  guarantee. `app/layout.tsx`'s `min-h-full flex flex-col` and `flex-1` are
  the same case. The standard as written is stricter than the diff that wrote
  it; someone should decide whether the standard means "no Tailwind for
  styling" or "no Tailwind at all," but not in this sprint.
- Disclaimer copy: keeping `DISCLAIMER_TEXT` and restyling only, rather than
  swapping in the handoff mockup's different wording, was the right call and
  the reasoning in Dev Notes is correct â€” legally reviewed text locked by a
  Sprint 1 test is not Dev Team's to change silently. Flagged to gate 4, which
  is where it belongs.
- `@media print { .no-print { display: none !important } }` exists at
  classical.css:280, and all three chrome elements carry `.no-print`. Whether
  it actually hides them is gate 2's measurement.
- No media queries were added anywhere; the out-of-scope "adding breakpoints"
  line is respected. Reflow is gate 2's.

===================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
===================================================================

Two Dev Notes corrections â€” issue 1 and issue 2 â€” and this is a PASS. No code
change, no test change, nothing to rebuild.

Then note what this sprint is carrying that the script cannot:

  **Gates 3 and 4 are not in the state machine.** `cmd_complete` checks
  `qa1_audit_result`, `groundtruth_result` and a non-empty `--user-said`, and
  nothing else. It will let this sprint close with the NVDA pass and Chang's
  legal review both unrecorded. The sprint file says this in its own
  acceptance criteria and says "do not discover it a third time." Sprint 9
  reached `complete_ready` with two green gates and a real defect. This sprint
  has two unmechanised gates instead of one, and one of them is a legal-content
  review on a product whose whole subject is statutory rights.

  **Gate 3's `/intake` regression check is the one that matters most.** Three
  sprints, five QA1 rounds and an abort went into those radiogroups. I have
  confirmed statically that nothing edited their markup and that no class name
  collides. That is not the same claim as Sprint 10's result still holding by
  ear under a new stylesheet, and only Chang can make the second one.

  **This diff touches ARIA** (`aria-current`, `aria-hidden`, the chrome
  landing on every route including intake). If GroundTruth or gate 3 comes
  back FAIL or CONDITIONAL and the fix touches ARIA attributes, roles, labels
  or accessible names, it gets an independent QA1 review of that diff recorded
  in Dev Notes before Pipeman reships â€” not the fast reship path.

The statute guard is the best thing in this diff and it is genuinely
fail-closed, genuinely wired, and genuinely exercised because someone thought
about why hand-authored candidates matter. Requirement 10 was turned into a
test instead of a promise. The disclaimer copy was left alone for the right
reason. What is missing is two paragraphs of honesty in Dev Notes about what
else the stylesheet reached and what else entered the repo.

PASS: PASS â€” QA1 audit round 2, Sprint 11, commit 1f69eae (HEAD), all audited paths
clean and committed (the only dirty file is sprint-7's definition, unrelated).
Sprint file re-read fresh before recording, and CLAUDE.md re-read at this
commit since this round amends it again.

Focused re-audit of an isolated correction, per the agent file: application
code is byte-identical to the commit I audited in round 1, the change is two
documentation edits, and the review concentrates there â€” but the gate-1
mechanical checks were re-run against this commit rather than carried forward.

SCOPE LIMIT, UNCHANGED
Static audit. Visual regression on `/intake`, contrast, reflow and print are
gate 2's, with real instruments. Announcements are gate 3's. Statute content
and authored copy are gate 4's. The cascade analysis below is read out of CSS
selectors and specificity, not off a rendered page.

===================================================================
WHAT MOVED, AND NOTHING ELSE DID
===================================================================

`git diff d735884 1f69eae` over `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` and
`package.json` is empty. The code I audited in round 1 is the code here. The
diff is CLAUDE.md's Stack paragraph, the sprint file's Dev Notes, and
`state/sprint-11.json` (my round-1 CONDITIONAL). No test changed; the suite is
110/110 across 16 files, `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint .` both exit 0, all re-run
at this commit.

===================================================================
ISSUE 1 â€” CLOSED, AND CORRECTLY
===================================================================

Both the CLAUDE.md paragraph and the Dev Notes finding were rewritten, and the
rewrite lands on the right distinction rather than bolting my example onto the
old framing.

CLAUDE.md now states the general rule: the Tailwind shield is **per property,
not per element** â€” "an element can carry Tailwind classes covering some of
its properties and still take every *other* property directly from
`classical.css`'s type-selector rules, because nothing shields what Tailwind
never set on that element in the first place." That is the accurate
formulation, and it subsumes the `p { margin }` and `a { color }` cases I
listed without needing to enumerate them. It then separates the two mechanisms
explicitly: inheritance for unstyled body text, direct type-selector match for
the `<h2>`. The specificity reasoning is still correct.

Dev Notes now splits the finding into the same two numbered cases and grounds
the second one in the source. I checked every factual claim in it rather than
accepting the correction because I asked for it:

- The `<h2>` at `components/IntakeFlow.tsx:760` does carry
  `className="font-medium text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-50"` with no font-size
  utility, and `app/classical.css:96` is `h2 { font-size: 32px }`. Direct
  type-selector match, as stated.
- "Its `font-medium`/`text-zinc-900` classes *do* still win for weight and
  color" â€” correct, those are class selectors setting those properties.
- The `<h1>` at line 849 claim is the one I expected to be loose, and it is
  exact. `classical.css:91-94` sets `font-family`, `font-weight`,
  `line-height: 1.12`, `letter-spacing: -0.015em` and
  `margin: 0 0 var(--space-2)` on `h1..h6`. `text-2xl font-semibold` covers
  size and weight only, so `font-family`, `line-height`, `letter-spacing` and
  `margin` do pass through â€” precisely the four properties Dev Notes names. It
  went and read the rule.

The overstated "colours are unaffected" sentence is gone rather than softened.

One imprecision, no action: the h2 is described as rendering at 32px "instead
of the browser's un-set default." Tailwind's preflight resets `h1..h6` to
`font-size: inherit`, so what it rendered at before was body size, not a UA
default. The substantive claim â€” 32px now, smaller before, by direct match â€” is
right, and nothing downstream is misdirected by the phrasing. Recording it so
it is clear I read the sentence rather than skimmed to the example.

===================================================================
ISSUE 2 â€” CLOSED
===================================================================

Dev Notes now carries a paragraph on committing `lib/guide.ts`, and its
reasoning is sound and checkable:

- That the file was already on disk at sprint start matches the sprint's own
  Dependencies note ("All three handoff files are on disk").
- That requirement 10 is "silent on whether the *file's presence* is in scope,
  only on whether anything *imports* it" is an accurate reading of the
  requirement's text and of the Out of Scope bullet, which defers relocation
  to "the sprint that first imports the file" â€” a sentence that presupposes
  the file persists in the repository.
- The handoff quotation is verbatim and correctly attributed:
  `docs/design-handoff.md:22-23` reads "The one exception is `lib/guide.ts`,
  which is **real, portable TypeScript** â€” pure data and logic with no UI.
  Drop it in as-is."
- "knowingly unimported â€” enforced mechanically by
  `lib/guide-import-boundary.test.ts`, not merely asserted" is the right
  emphasis and it is true: grep confirms zero imports across `app/`,
  `components/` and `lib/`, and the test asserts the absence per file.

The 428-line file entering the repo is now something a reader finds in Dev
Notes rather than in `git show --stat`, which is all I asked for.

STILL OPEN FOR MASTER CONTROLLER, and still not blocking. The gate-1 criterion
"no domain-shaped interface is declared outside `lib/types.ts`" and the
requirement-10 deferral point different ways now that the file is in the
repository. I have twice read the specific deferral as governing the general
criterion, and Dev Team's paragraph gives the same reading â€” but Dev Team
adopting an auditor's reading is not the same as the requirement saying it.
Per Sprint 10's Amendment 1, a criterion that fires on something the same
document deliberately permits gets settled by amendment, not by two people
agreeing in Dev Notes. One sentence in requirement 10 would close it for good.

===================================================================
THE ELEVEN GATE-1 CHECKS, RE-RUN AT 1f69eae
===================================================================

All pass, as in round 1, and re-verified rather than carried forward:

1. `classical.css` imported exactly once, globally (`app/layout.tsx:7`).
2. No hard-coded hex and no px literal duplicating a declared spacing or
   radius token in any new or modified component.
3. CLAUDE.md's Project Standards updated in this sprint's diff, and now
   accurate as well as present.
4. No file imports `lib/guide.ts`; the boundary test enforces it.
5. The statute guard fails closed on every path â€” empty library, non-object,
   null, missing id, unlisted id, drifted text â€” with no throw, no swallow and
   no reachable default-pass branch.
6. `STATUTE_REFERENCE_LIBRARY` is a named export and every `/about` row
   renders only via `result.reference`, with a visible withheld notice on the
   failure branch. Candidates are hand-authored so the guard can actually
   fail.
7. No domain-shaped interface in this sprint's own code outside
   `lib/types.ts`; `StatuteReference` is in it, `StatuteCitationGuardResult`
   sits beside its guard exactly as `CitationGuardResult` does.
8. `aria-current` wired from `usePathname()` with strict equality and
   `undefined` rather than `"false"`.
9. Both decorative numeral sets carry `aria-hidden="true"`, inside their
   `.map()`s so every instance is covered.
10. Vitest 110/110 across 16 files, including all three requirement-11 cases
    and five more; no render-assertion test, no `jsdom`/`happy-dom`/
    `@testing-library` anywhere.
11. No file under `app/intake/` modified â€” nor `components/IntakeFlow.tsx`,
    where the markup actually lives. Re-confirmed against Sprint 10's closing
    commit, not just against round 1. The class-name collision check I ran in
    round 1 still holds: none of `classical.css`'s 36 class selectors appear
    in intake's markup.

===================================================================
ISSUES FOUND
===================================================================

None blocking. Two things carried forward unchanged, neither a fix:

1. `components/DisclaimerBanner.tsx` mixes `classical.css` classes with
   Tailwind utilities (`sticky top-0 z-50`) in one component, as does
   `app/layout.tsx`, which the CLAUDE.md paragraph calls "what this split
   exists to avoid." `.disclaimer` sets no positioning, so those utilities
   supply behaviour the stylesheet lacks and preserve Sprint 1's sticky
   guarantee. I said in round 1 this was not a fix for this sprint and it
   still is not; someone should eventually decide whether the standard means
   "no Tailwind for styling" or "no Tailwind at all," but not under this
   sprint's clock.
2. `/about` and the landing page are styled largely through inline `style`
   objects rather than the component-class layer this sprint landed, with
   every value routed through tokens. Passes every criterion as written. A
   design-system adherence question for whoever owns the next screen.

===================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
===================================================================

Gate 1 is closed. Dev Team runs `/sprint-dev-done`, Pipeman ships.

Three things travel with this PASS:

  1. DO NOT EDIT THE SPRINT FILE BETWEEN THIS PASS AND `/sprint-dev-done`.
     This PASS records a hash of the file as audited, and `dev_done` refuses
     outright, no override, if it changes. Re-audit rather than routing
     around it; that refusal is the check working.

  2. THIS DIFF TOUCHES ARIA and lands global CSS on every route including
     `/intake`. If GroundTruth or gate 3 comes back FAIL or CONDITIONAL and
     the fix touches ARIA attributes, roles, labels or accessible names, it
     gets an independent QA1 review of that diff recorded in Dev Notes before
     Pipeman reships â€” not the fast reship path.

  3. GATES 3 AND 4 ARE NOT IN THE STATE MACHINE. `cmd_complete` checks
     `qa1_audit_result`, `groundtruth_result` and a non-empty `--user-said`,
     and nothing else. It will let this sprint close with Chang's NVDA pass
     and Chang's legal review both unrecorded. The sprint file says so in its
     own acceptance criteria and says "do not discover it a third time."
     Sprint 9 reached `complete_ready` on two green gates and its third gate
     then found a real defect. Here there are two unmechanised gates, and one
     of them is a legal-content review on a product whose subject is statutory
     rights â€” the statute table, the disclaimer wording, the landing page's
     "most of these situations are workable," and the ESA s. 74 / ss. 50-56
